title.rendered: Father, I Thank You That You Heard Me: Thanks Before the Miracle | The Thankful Heart, Day 4

excerpt.rendered: John 11:41-42: Jesus gave thanks before Lazarus walked out of the tomb. Day 4 of The Thankful Heart learns to thank God before we see the answer.

content.rendered:
Lazarus was still in the tomb when Jesus said thank You. He did not wait for the stone to roll or the dead man to walk. He gave thanks first, because He knew the Father had already heard.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, November 18, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 4

Today’s Scripture

“And Jesus lifted up His eyes and said, ‘Father, I thank You that You have heard Me. And I know that You always hear Me, but because of the people who are standing by I said this, that they may believe that You sent Me.’”
John 11:41-42 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Picture the scene at Bethany. Lazarus has been dead four days. Martha and Mary are grieving. The mourners are weeping. Jesus Himself has wept. The stone has just been rolled away from the tomb, and everyone is waiting to see what He will do. What He does first is give thanks.

“Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.” Notice the tense. Not “I will thank You if You hear Me.” Not “I will thank You once Lazarus walks out.” Jesus thanks the Father in the past tense, while the body is still wrapped in graveclothes. In His heart the answer was already settled. The miracle that followed was simply the outward evidence of what He had already thanked God for.

Then He tells us why: “And I know that You always hear Me.” This was not a technique. It was the overflow of a relationship. Jesus knew the Father. He knew the Father’s heart, His will and His faithfulness. Thanksgiving before the miracle is what confidence in a good Father sounds like.

Here is the good news for us. In Christ we share that same standing. Scripture tells us that all the promises of God in Him are Yes, and in Him Amen (2 Corinthians 1:20). John writes that if we know He hears us, we know that we have what we have asked of Him (1 John 5:14-15). So when we give thanks before we see the answer, we are not pretending. We are agreeing with what God has already said and already given in His Son.

Is there a situation in your life that still looks like a closed tomb? A diagnosis in Nairobi, a delayed visa in Manila, a prodigal child in London? Before you see the stone move, try lifting your eyes as Jesus did and saying, “Father, I thank You that You have heard me.” You are not forcing God’s hand. You are resting in His heart. Thanks offered in advance is faith speaking out loud.

How the Thankful Heart Believes

It thanks God before the evidence. Jesus said thank You while Lazarus was still in the tomb.

It rests on relationship, not on technique. “I know that You always hear Me” is the voice of a Son who knows his Father.

It agrees with what God has already said. In Christ every promise is Yes, so thanksgiving is our Amen.

Declaration

Father, I thank You that You hear me, because I come to You in the name of Your Son (John 16:23). I thank You that all Your promises in Christ are Yes and Amen (2 Corinthians 1:20). Before I see the answer, I lift my eyes and give thanks, because You are faithful and You have already provided everything I need in Jesus. I do not wait for the stone to move to praise You. I thank You now. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
